paper.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
paper.authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandara Piktus, et al.
paper.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2020)
paper.abstract: We explore general-purpose fine-tuning recipes for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) — models which combine pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory for language generation. We evaluate RAG models on a wide range of knowledge-intensive NLP benchmarks, showing state-of-the-art results on open-domain QA and reduced hallucination compared to purely parametric models.
passages: RAG models combine pre-trained parametric memory with non-parametric retrieval. In open-domain question answering, retrieval augmentation reduced hallucination rates and outperformed standard sequence-to-sequence fine-tuning on Natural Questions.

claim_verification_cases.claim_text: RAG models suffered higher hallucination rates than purely parametric models on open-domain question answering benchmarks.

paper.title: A Systematic Review of Calcium Signaling Pathways in Cardiac Myocytes
paper.abstract: Calcium homeostasis is essential for electromechanical coupling in cardiac myocytes. This review examines ryanodine receptor activation and sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase regulation under physiological and pathological conditions.
passages: Ryanodine receptors mediate rapid calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum during systole.

research_question: Analyze parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods including LoRA and QLoRA for large language models.

paper.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
paper.authors: Tim Dettmers, Artidoro Pagnoni, Ari Holtzman, Luke Zettlemoyer
paper.abstract: We present QLoRA, an efficient finetuning approach that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance. QLoRA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters (LoRA).
passages: QLoRA introduces 4-bit NormalFloat quantization, double quantization, and paged optimizers, reducing the memory footprint of 65B model fine-tuning from >780GB to <48GB of VRAM.

claim_verification_cases.claim_text: QLoRA enables fine-tuning of 65 billion parameter models on a single 48GB GPU by quantizing weights to 4-bit NormalFloat precision.
claim_verification_cases.evidence_passage: QLoRA introduces 4-bit NormalFloat quantization, double quantization, and paged optimizers, reducing the memory footprint of 65B model fine-tuning from >780GB to <48GB of VRAM.

claim_verification_cases.claim_text: QLoRA eliminates all memory bottlenecks and speeds up model training by 10x over full fine-tuning across all hardware architectures.
claim_verification_cases.evidence_passage: QLoRA reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance.

paper.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
paper.authors: Edward Hu, Yelong Shen, Phillip Wallis, et al.
paper.abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation, or LoRA, freezes pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture, greatly reducing the number of trainable parameters for downstream tasks.
passages: LoRA reduces the number of trainable parameters by 10,000 times and GPU memory requirements by 3 times compared to GPT-3 175B full fine-tuning.

claim_verification_cases.claim_text: LoRA freezes pre-trained Transformer weights and trains low-rank decomposition matrices, reducing trainable parameters up to 10,000 times on GPT-3 175B.
claim_verification_cases.evidence_passage: LoRA reduces the number of trainable parameters by 10,000 times and GPU memory requirements by 3 times compared to GPT-3 175B full fine-tuning.

research_question: Examine the macroeconomic impact of generative AI automation on high-skill labor markets, wages, and productivity dispersion.

paper.title: Generative AI at Work: Productivity Effects in Customer Support
paper.authors: Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li, Lindsey R. Raymond
paper.abstract: We study the phased implementation of a generative AI-based conversational assistant across 5,179 customer support agents. AI assistance increases worker productivity by 14% on average, with the largest gains observed among novice and low-skill workers.
passages: Access to the generative AI tool increases resolution rates by 14% and reduces resolution times, with substantial acceleration for workers in the bottom skill quartile.

claim_verification_cases.claim_text: Generative AI assistance increased customer support agent productivity by 14% on average, delivering the greatest benefits to low-skill workers.
claim_verification_cases.evidence_passage: Access to the generative AI tool increases resolution rates by 14% and reduces resolution times, with substantial acceleration for workers in the bottom skill quartile.
